subject: Zero-Inflated N-Mixture: Simulated data works but real does not

messages.author: 7e5b5ac76117f50b
messages.subject: Zero-Inflated N-Mixture: Simulated data works but real does not
parts:
Hello all,

I am working on a integrated N-Mixture model which combines various citizen science point count surveys to estimate relative abundance across an area of interest, similar to the model described here: https://doi.org/10.1111/ddi.13416. I have constructed a base model which uses 2 surveys to estimate abundance ("lambda") and occurrence ("psi", zero-inflation term) across a sampling grid, with independent detection rate metrics for each survey. The model runs as intended with simulated data, however, when I apply the model to real data with the same structure, I have consistent issues. These include the model returning "missing values (NAs) or non-finite values" for lambda/psi when initializing ("$initializeInfo()"), returning LogProb = -Inf ("$calculate()"), and the sampler sticks to the initial starting values. I reviewed the input data as I suspect this must be the issue, but the real and simulated data follow the same general structure and there are no missing values. 

I am relatively new to nimble and don't have the most experience interpreting errors and trouble shooting. If anyone has any suggestions it would be greatly appreciated. I have included the relevant R files below and have included the general model code below. As a note, I am created a zero-inflated poisson nimble function as described here (https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/zero_inflated_poisson.html, where dZIP calls the relevant distribution within the model) which is called via sourcing an r script which I have also provided.

ZIPcode <- nimbleCode({  
  for (i in 1:1000){
    cloglog(psi[i]) <- alpha0 + alpha1*cov1[i]
    log(lambda[i]) <- beta0 + beta1*cov1[i]
   
    N[i] ~ dZIP(lambda[i], zeroProb = 1-psi[i])
   
    E.2[i] <- gamma2*cov3[i]
    p.2[i] <- 1 - (.5)^E.2[i]
   
    y.2[i] ~ dbinom(size = N[i], prob = p.2[i])  
   
  }
 
  for(i in 1:500){
    E.1[i] <- gamma1*cov2[i]
    p.1[i] <- 1 - (.5)^E.1[i]
   
    y.1[i] ~ dbinom(size = N[surv.id1[i]], prob = p.1[i])
   
  }
 
  alpha0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  beta0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  alpha1 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  beta1 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  gamma1 ~ T(dnorm(0,0.0001), 0,1000)
  gamma2 ~ T(dnorm(0,0.0001), 0,10000)
}) 

I appreciate any insights or potential solutions for me to pursue. Thanks,
Matt

messages.author: 7e5b5ac76117f50b
messages.subject: Re: Zero-Inflated N-Mixture: Simulated data works but real does not
parts: Just following up, the issue has been resolved. It was an initial values issue. My gamma's were too high, leading to a p == 1 in the dbinom of surveys, which resulted in issues when  N != y.

Dear Matt,
Thanks for posting a clear reproducible example.  And apologies we didn't get to it more quickly.  And now thanks for posting your solution!  The cases like p==1 and p==0 from initial values have caused confusions before and understandably so.  Please post again if you get stuck.
Perry
